newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian golds regroup as bullion beating abates.
newsitem.headline: Australian golds regroup as bullion beating abates.

text.p: Australian gold stocks headed to the upside for the first time in five sessions on Wednesday with the gold index gaining 2.8 percent in early trade.
Normandy Mining, the sector heavyweight constituting over 20 percent of the gold index, added nearly four percent to A$1.33.

Among others, Plutonic Resources climbed about three percent to A$3.50, Sons of Gwalia jumped 5.7 percent to A$4.65, Acacia Resources rose 3.9 percent to A$1.34, while Great Central Mines was up nearly two percent at A$2.19.
Newcrest Mining, beset by problems at its high cost Telfer mine in Western Australia, firmed early to A$2.71 but had drifted four cents lower to A$2.60 by 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT).
While the uptick was greeted with relief by traders, they said investor enthusiasm was likely to be muted as a keen watch was kept on gyrations in the bullion market.
"It will take while before we see investor confidence come back into this end of the market," said a senior dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Even with today's bounceback, losses sustained by the gold index since July 2 amount to nearly 17 percent with few analysts confident in a quick comeback in the precious metals price.
"There are problems there," said a resource analyst at a Sydney brokerage, citing negative sentiment and the numbers of short positions held by traders.
"The trend is still down for gold. It's just a matter of just wait and see where it bottoms."
